title: Playhouse and Harold Batiste
summary: Working the Playhouse with Harold Batiste, his tenor sax, and later California writing and a New Orleans studio.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Was there a place called the Playhouse or the Playboy or something like that around?

Yeah. Yeah, I played the, I think with the, not the Playboy, I think with the, the Playhouse I used to work at on, I think it was St. Louis and Bourbon. And me and Bob Ostens, another good musician, Harold. What does Harold play? Harold played saxophone.
What kind of sax was he playing then?
He would play at Big Sack, what they call it, the tenor. Yeah. He had a tenor sax. He played, he played Clown that too, but he never worried much. He looked great, he was a great musician though.
Did he ever write any pieces in?

Well they tell me he writing for some big outfit in California now, you know, which you know, him and Melvin Batiste, Melvin Lestey, they had a recording studio, real, I mean, real well-equipped, yeah, right here in New Orleans. Do you remember that?
He was, Harold Batiste was with Sonny and Sheriff on the one.
Yeah, he wrote some things for that.
